messages:
Maria (support): Customer corp-acme just escalated — they got 7 alerts in a 10m window for 'high-ingest-rate' but their request logs show no traffic spike. charts show a big, short spike around 03:00 UTC. billing reported a correlated cost bump. link: https://console.redwood/metrics/dash/abcd

Devin (eng-sre): can you paste the alert definition and a screenshot? also which model/route is this for?

Maria (support): alert definition: `when sum(agg_count_v2) over 5m > 10000` — it's org-scoped for corp-acme. screenshot: (attached). The spike is narrow and looks like aggregation noise, not real requests.

Chris (telemetry): looking at ingestion logs for corp-acme around 02:55–03:05 UTC. I see a reprocess job that touched old batches:
```
2026-03-10T03:01:12Z rollup-worker INFO reprocess batch id=bbf3 range=2026-03-10T02:55:00Z-2026-03-10T03:00:00Z items=1200
2026-03-10T03:01:12Z rollup-worker DEBUG emitting bucket=2026-03-10T03:00:00Z count=1200
```
Some of those events have event_time from an earlier window but are being assigned into the 03:00 bucket.

Alyssa (product-analytics): so duplicates getting pushed into the recent bucket and the 5m sum sees a transient jump. that would explain alert fires and the billing blip.

Devin (eng-sre): quick scan of rollup-worker code: there's a bucket calc that uses `ceil(event_ts / 300) * 300` — that will push boundary events forward into the next 5m bucket instead of the intended floor alignment. if reprocessing runs, old events can shift into the current bucket.

Devin (eng-sre): snippet from the offending code:
```python
# bug: shifts borderline timestamps forward
bucket = math.ceil(event_ts / 300) * 300  # wrong
# expected behavior:
bucket = math.floor(event_ts / 300) * 300
```

Chris (telemetry): confirming: reprocess job also lacked idempotency checks for the same event id -> same event can be aggregated twice when combined with the boundary bug. two bugs compounding.

Maria (support): customer is furious — they're seeing both alerts and a short-term billing spike. I've temporarily muted alerts for their org and told them we're investigating.

Devin (eng-sre): immediate actions: 1) hotfix rollup-worker to use floor and add idempotency check; 2) pause reprocess queue for affected time ranges; 3) create backfill to recompute the 02:45–03:10 windows with corrected logic; 4) add a short-term alert suppression rule for orgs affected by backfills. I'll open a PR now.

Chris (telemetry): I'll run a dry backfill on staging with the fixed code and compare sums vs current. If results match expected (no phantom spikes), we can schedule prod backfill. Also adding a one-time dedupe pass for events with duplicate event_id + org.

rollup-bot: deploy started: rollup-worker v1.12.4-hotfix -> staging

Devin (eng-sre): PR #4729 opened with tests for boundary behavior and idempotency. tagging @chris for telemetry tests.

Chris (telemetry): staging dry-run shows the phantom spike disappears when we use floor + dedupe. prod patch queued.

Devin (eng-sre): deployed hotfix to prod and paused reprocess queue for 02:40–03:20. monitoring dashboards show the 5m alert metric returned to baseline by 03:12 UTC.

Maria (support): notified corp-acme of the fix and offered a billing review. they asked for postmortem + ETA for backfill.

Alyssa (product-analytics): please include mitigation steps in the postmortem (muting alerts, pause reprocess, backfill plan) and add a flag we can flip to prevent automated reprocesses for orgs in 'billing_review' state.

Devin (eng-sre): will do. follow-ups: postmortem, PR merge, prod backfill this evening during low-traffic window, add regression test to prevent ceil->floor regressions.

Maria (support): thanks team :thumbsup: will keep customer updated.
